messages.subject: Factor analysis project participation
parts:
Hello!
I'm a third-year student of the Department of Applied Math at Saint-Petersburg State University. I'm interested in the project idea "Factor models for return series". I have a solid background in math and probability theory, also I have an extensive experience in programming using different programming languages (from C++ to Common Lisp). Moreover I've successfully finished last year GSOC. But my experience with R is not so great - I'm only using it for about a half of a year. Also I don't have much experience in economics - just a couple of courses in micro and macroeconomics and computational finance. But I'm really interested in this field and ready to work really hard to close the gap in knowledge. 
So my questions are - what I should do to increase my chances to be accepted for the project? What direction should I go first? With whom can I discuss details about project? I've tried to contact Eric Zivot (project mentor) directly, but it looks like my message went to spam or something.
Thanks in advance!
